business_problem: Zuoyebang needed low-cost, scalable storage and analytics for TB-scale application and user-behavior data generated by a very large student learning platform.
solution_summary: Zuoyebang used Baidu AI Cloud to build a cloud-native data platform for educational application analytics. The workflow starts with BLS log services collecting application and behavior data directly from servers using a lightweight hosted architecture that minimizes operational effort. Those logs are stored in BOS object storage, which provides low-cost, scalable and secure storage without transfer fees into Baidu's processing environment. Scheduled cleansing and filtering are then executed through Baidu MapReduce, a fully managed Hadoop and Spark cluster service that can scale up or down with demand while staying inside a private network. After cleaning, the data is written into downstream databases and reporting systems, with a scheduling layer monitoring the overall platform. The result is a classic modern data pipeline—collection, storage, processing and reporting—but delivered as managed services so Zuoyebang can focus on educational products rather than operating a large in-house analytics stack.

solution_components.name: MapReduce
solution_components.role: Runs scheduled filtering and cleaning jobs over large educational datasets.

solution_components.name: BOS Object Storage
solution_components.role: Stores large application and behavior datasets at low cost.

solution_components.name: BLS Log Service
solution_components.role: Collects application and behavior logs from servers as the ingestion layer.

solution_components.name: Task Scheduling System
solution_components.role: Monitors and manages the jobs that make up the data platform.

data_flow: User activity and application logs are collected by BLS, stored in BOS, processed by MapReduce jobs for cleansing and statistics, and then written into downstream reporting systems under scheduler supervision.
business_outcome: Zuoyebang obtained a managed analytics foundation for ETL, statistics and query workloads while lowering the operational burden and cost of running a large student-data platform.
metrics: The platform had more than 130 million users and roughly 60% share of the photo-problem-solving market as of 2016.

BOS to BMR data transfer is part of the cost-optimized design
